_review: Meadow side quests and shrines (user request 2026-10-24: more side quests, quest direction on the HUD). Merged into the chapter data by systems/chapter.js (mergeChapters). Ids are meadow-side-*; flags are meadow:side-*. Dialogue follows docs/village/dialogue-style.md. Places carry their mechanics' data (rings, stones' gestures); the sites stand where tools/world/sample.mjs found dry, level ground (tests/sideQuests.test.js pins that). Mechanics: systems/sideQuests.js.
title: The Burning Night

npcs.name: Ketil
npcs.about: Keeper of the lamps of Hearn. Lights the Fen Lamp's flame for the Wraith.

npcs.name: Orm
npcs.about: Stonewright. The ninth stone of the ring has lain on its side since the great calm.

npcs.name: Dunn
npcs.about: Farmer north of the village. Something hides in his barley.

npcs.name: Wyl
npcs.about: Courier of Hearn. Set six rings along the Western Edge for gliders.

npcs.name: Maud
npcs.about: Weaver. Her grandmother taught her to listen to the three stones on the lake shore.

meadow.ketil.busy.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: I am Ketil, keeper of the lamps of Hearn.
I cannot talk now. The fires come first.

meadow.ketil.plea.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: I am Ketil. I keep the lamps of Hearn.
The Fen Lamp stands on the north shore of the lake, where the path bends away from the water. It went dark on the night of the raid.
Without it, people lose the path in the reeds after dark. Two have walked into the water this month.
It needs a flame from my hearth. Come to me after dark, and I will light your lantern.

meadow.ketil.dark.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: The lamp is lit at night. Come back after dark, and I will light your lantern.

meadow.ketil.flame.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: Hold out your lantern. There.
Carry it to the Fen Lamp, on the north shore of the lake. Walk. If you run, the flame gutters.
A blow will put it out, and so will a hard wind. If it dies, come back and I will light it again.

meadow.ketil.relight.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: It went out? It happens. Hold out your lantern again.
The Fen Lamp is on the north shore. Keep the flame low.

meadow.ketil.wait.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: The Fen Lamp is on the north shore, west along the lake. Walk, and shelter the flame from the wind.

meadow.ketil.done.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: I can see it from my door. The Fen Lamp is burning.
Thank you. The path is safe again. My mother said the lamp was lit for the people who cannot see the way, and for the ones who can.

meadow.ketil.after.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: The Fen Lamp burns every night now. Thank you.

meadow.orm.busy.speaker: meadow-orm
lines: I am Orm, a stonewright.
I have a job that needs the wind. Come back when you can call it.

meadow.orm.plea.speaker: meadow-orm
lines: I am Orm, stonewright of Hearn. There is a ring of nine standing stones on the flat south-east of the hall.
The ninth fell in the great calm. It has lain on its side ever since. Ten men could not lift it.
You have the Gale now. An Updraft can lift it, but only a little at a time.
Cast one at the head of the stone, one at the middle and one at the foot. Do all three before it settles.

meadow.orm.wait.speaker: meadow-orm
lines: The ring is south-east of the hall, on the flat above the stair road.
Take the Gale in hand, and cast Updraft at the head, the middle and the foot of the fallen stone.

meadow.orm.done.speaker: meadow-orm
lines: It stands! I felt it from here. The ground rang.
Nine stones again. Thank you. Go to the ring at noon, and the shadows fall the way my grandfather meant them to.

meadow.orm.after.speaker: meadow-orm
lines: The ring is whole. I sit with it most evenings.

meadow.dunn.busy.speaker: meadow-dunn
lines: I am Dunn. I farm the barley north of Hearn.
Not now. Your fires first.

meadow.dunn.plea.speaker: meadow-dunn
lines: I am Dunn. I farm the barley north of Hearn. Something is living in it.
Three ewes gone in a week. I found tracks like long bird feet, and plaited stalks. Hild says they are Sedgerunners.
They lie still in the barley until you are almost on them. Then they all break at once.
Walk through the field, flush them out, and put them down.

meadow.dunn.wait.speaker: meadow-dunn
lines: The barley is straight north, past the last houses. Walk right into it. They only break when you are close.

meadow.dunn.done.speaker: meadow-dunn
lines: The barley is quiet. I can hear the wind in it and nothing else.
Take this. My wife wove it from the first sheaf of the year. It is a barley cloak.

meadow.dunn.after.speaker: meadow-dunn
lines: The ewes are back in the north field. Nothing has touched them.

meadow.wyl.busy.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: I am Wyl. I carry messages between Hearn and the farms.
I would rather fly them.

meadow.wyl.plea.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: I am Wyl, courier of Hearn. You can glide now. I saw you on the hill.
I set six rings along the Western Edge, past the lake road, where the ground falls away.
Jump off the edge, hold your robe open and fly through all six. I keep the time.
Under thirty seconds is bronze. Twenty-five is silver. Twenty-one is gold.

meadow.wyl.wait.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: The Western Edge is due west, past the lake road. Run off the crest, jump, and hold the glide.
Take the rings in order. The first one is just below the crest.

meadow.wyl.bronze.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: Bronze. Not bad for a walker. Silver is under twenty-five seconds.
Dive between the rings to carry your speed.

meadow.wyl.silver.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: Silver! You are faster than I am. Gold is under twenty-one seconds.
Take the line straight through the rings, and do not bank more than you must.

meadow.wyl.gold.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: Gold! Under twenty-one seconds. I have never done that.
You have earned the courier's cloth. I made it from the sail of my first kite.

meadow.wyl.after.speaker: meadow-wyl
lines: I fly it every morning, and every morning I am slower than you.

meadow.maud.busy.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: I am Maud, a weaver.
I listen to the old stones by the lake. They have been silent since the wind stopped.

meadow.maud.plea.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: I am Maud, a weaver. My grandmother taught me to listen to the three stones on the lake shore.
They did not speak in the calm. Now the wind is back, and I think they are asking for something.
Go and listen to them. Each wants the wind shaped in a certain way: a Gust, a Vortex, an Updraft. Do what each one asks, in order.

meadow.maud.wait.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: The stones are on the east shore of the lake, west of the village. Press E at a stone and listen. Then shape the wind as it asks.

meadow.maud.attune.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: I heard them sing from my loom! They gave you an Echo.
Rest at a shrine to carry it. The Green Shrine, on the village green, is the nearest. Attune it there.

meadow.maud.done.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: The wind came from nowhere when you attuned it. I felt it in the loom threads.
My grandmother said the stones remember the first Shapers. Now they remember you.

meadow.maud.after.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: The stones hum in the evening now. I leave my window open.

quests.title: The Fen Lamp
quests.summary: Ketil keeps the lamps of Hearn. The Fen Lamp on the lake shore has gone dark, and people lose the path at night.

steps.journal: Talk to Ketil, the lamp-keeper, in Hearn.
Go to Ketil after dark. He will light your lantern.
Carry the flame to the Fen Lamp on the north shore of the lake. Walk, and keep it out of the wind. If it dies, go back to Ketil.
Tell Ketil the Fen Lamp is lit.

quests.title: The Fallen Stone
quests.summary: Orm the stonewright has a ring of nine standing stones. The ninth fell in the great calm, and only the wind can lift it.

steps.journal: Talk to Orm, the stonewright, in Hearn.
Go to the Ring of Nine, on the flat south-east of the hall.
Raise the fallen stone. Take the Gale in hand (2) and cast Updraft (F) at its head, its middle and its foot, one after another.
Tell Orm the stone stands.

quests.title: The Flock in the Barley
quests.summary: Something hides in Dunn's barley and takes his ewes.

steps.journal: Talk to Dunn, the farmer, in Hearn.
Go to Dunn's barley, north of the village.
Walk through the barley. The Sedgerunners hide in it and break when you come close. Put them all down.
Tell Dunn the barley is quiet.

quests.title: The Western Edge
quests.summary: Wyl the courier set six rings down the slope west of the lake road. Glide through them, and he keeps the time.

steps.journal: Talk to Wyl, the courier, in Hearn.
Go to the Western Edge, past the lake road. The first ring hangs just below the crest.
Glide through all six rings in under 30 seconds. Run off the crest, jump, and hold the glide.
Glide the rings in under 25 seconds. Dive between them to keep your speed.
Glide the rings in under 21 seconds. Take the straight line through them.
Tell Wyl your time.

quests.title: The Stones That Listen
quests.summary: Maud the weaver says three stones on the lake shore are asking for something, now that the wind is back.

steps.journal: Talk to Maud, the weaver, in Hearn.
Go to the three Listening Stones on the east shore of the lake, west of the village.
Answer all three stones. Press E at a stone, then shape the wind as it asks: Gust (click), Vortex (hold click) or Updraft (F), in order.
Rest at a shrine and attune the Echo. The Green Shrine is on the village green.
Tell Maud the stones answered.

echo-meadow-wind.name: Echo of the Turning Wind
echo-meadow-wind.effect: Gust runs 30% farther, and the Updraft's column rises 25% higher.
echo-meadow-wind.text: The stones taught the wind to answer.

meadow-lore-fen.title: The Fen Lamp
meadow-lore-fen.text: Ketil's mother lit the Fen Lamp every dusk for forty years. She said a lamp is lit for the people who cannot see the way, and for the ones who can. As told by Ketil.

meadow-lore-ring.title: The Ring of Nine
meadow-lore-ring.text: Nine stones stand on the flat above the stair road, set by Orm's grandfather. At noon on the longest day their shadows meet in the middle. As told by Orm.

meadow-lore-barley.title: The Hidden Flock
meadow-lore-barley.text: Sedgerunners lie still in tall grass and break all at once when something comes close. They are lean, and light enough that a Gust bowls them over. As told by Dunn.

meadow-lore-edge.title: The Western Edge
meadow-lore-edge.text: West of the lake road the ground falls away for a long way. Wyl's six rings hang over it, and the wind comes up the slope. As told by Wyl.

meadow-lore-listening.title: The Listening Stones
meadow-lore-listening.text: Three stones stand on the east shore of the lake. They were set to answer the wind, and in the calm they had nothing to answer. As told by Maud.

lines: I look at the Fen Lamp every night before I sleep.
Mind the reeds if you walk the shore tonight.
Wick, oil, flint. That is all a lamp is.
Nine. I count them every morning.
A stone is only heavy if you push it the wrong way.
Quiet barley. I never thought I would miss the noise.
Something moves in my barley when the wind is still.
Six rings, and you took them all. I am not jealous. A little.
If I had your robe I would never touch the ground.
The stones hum in the evening now.
Hush. Do you hear that? No. It was the loom.
